chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the one who does not recite the Opening of the Book in his prayer. He said, 'There is no prayer for him unless he recites it in audibility or concealment.' For the intended meaning is that if he does not recite it intentionally, without forgetfulness, then there is no prayer for him. As for with forgetfulness, then his prayer is valid.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer if one forgets to recite Al-Fatiha?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the condition of Fatiha recitation in prayer, distinguishing between intentional omission which invalidates the prayer and forgetfulness which does not. It underscores the scholarly consensus that Fatiha is a pillar (rukn) of the prayer, yet its absence due to error is excused, reflecting the balance between strict adherence and divine mercy in Shia fiqh. The narration emphasizes that the requirement applies regardless of whether the recitation is in a loud or quiet prayer.
